sections.h2: What does the Nash County Register of Deeds keep on file?
sections.html:
The office holds land records going back to 1777, the year Nash County was carved out of Edgecombe County. Marriage records start in 1862, and birth and death records begin in October 1913.

Deeds from 1777 through 1969 are searchable online. Anything newer is available as a hard copy, so a seller hunting for an old deed of trust or a plat should ring the office at (252) 459-9836, the number shown on the county's e-recording page. A Nash County deed of trust or deed that predates 1970 can often be found without leaving home.

sections.h2: Is a house in Rocky Mount recorded in Nash County?
sections.html:
Sometimes, and sometimes in Edgecombe County. The county's health report says Rocky Mount straddles the Nash and Edgecombe line, while the rest of Nash County is largely rural. Check the tax parcel record for the lot before a deed is drafted.

Nash County sits in the northeast part of the state and borders Edgecombe, Wilson, Johnston, Franklin and Halifax Counties. Its eleven municipalities fall into five areas:

  • County seat: Nashville
  • East: Rocky Mount and Sharpsburg
  • North: Dortches, Castalia, Red Oak and Whitakers
  • South: Middlesex and Bailey
  • West: Momeyer and Spring Hope

A seller in Spring Hope and a seller in Sharpsburg record at the same county office, even though the towns lie at opposite ends of the county.

sections.h2: How should a deed be printed for Nash County?
sections.html:
The county's filing standards page turns the state paper rules into a short checklist for anything recorded on or after July 1, 2002. A deed that falls short is still accepted, but with a $25.00 nonstandard fee added.

  • Letter size (8 1/2 by 11) or legal size (8 1/2 by 14) paper.
  • Three inches of blank space at the top of page one.
  • Dark type on white stock, 10 points or larger.
  • Print on a single side of each sheet.
  • The instrument type placed beneath the blank top margin.

Blanks can be filled by pen. The county's note says the margin on the other edges of page one shrank to one quarter inch on October 1, 2011. Where the type is under 10 points but still readable, the Register may waive the extra charge.

sections.h2: What fees does the Nash County Register of Deeds list for real estate?
sections.html:
The county's 2025-2026 fee schedule prints the real estate charges below. The first four match the statewide amounts in G.S. 161-10, and the rest are line items a seller or closing attorney may meet along the way.

Real estate fees from the Nash County 2025-2026 fee schedule, Register of Deeds section
ItemFee
Instruments in general, first 15 pages$26.00, then $4.00 per added page
Deed of trust, first 35 pages$64.00, then $4.00 per added page
Plat, each sheet$21.00

Source: Nash County Fee Schedule. The same schedule lists excise stamps at $1.00 per $500.

sections.h2: Who pays the excise stamps when a Nash County house sells?
sections.html:
The seller. The schedule shows stamps at $1.00 per $500, and G.S. 105-228.30 puts the duty on the transferor, due before the deed is recorded. It applies to each fraction of $500 as well.

On the settlement statement this appears as a seller cost, and it is a separate item from any income tax on the gain. Ask the closing attorney to show the stamp line when you review the draft statement, since the amount follows the price on the deed.

sections.h2: How do you e-record a deed in Nash County?
sections.html:
A filer signs a Memorandum of Understanding and then receives a filing number. The county's phone for that step is (252) 459-9836.

Electronic recordings are received from 8:00 am to 4:30 pm on weekdays, holidays excluded. Closing attorneys and title firms are the usual filers, so a seller's job is mostly to sign on time and ask which day the deed was submitted.

sections.h2: What if a Nash County lot has to be split before a sale?
sections.html:
The county's planning fees show how much that adds. A recombination or exempt plat costs $25, a minor final plat of two lots or fewer with no road, water, sewer or drainage work costs $50 plus $10 per lot, and a zoning permit is $10. The schedule adds that recording fees for plats are paid to the Register of Deeds when the plat is approved.

New construction or additions inside Bailey, Castalia, Dortches, Middlesex, Momeyer, Nashville, Red Oak, Sharpsburg, Spring Hope or Whitakers also need a zoning permit from that town's office before the county issues construction permits. A buyer who wants to add a room should know that before closing.

A recorded plat sheet costs $21.00 to file, and the county's tax office sells recorded plat copies at $4.00 for a full-size sheet and $1.00 for a reduced one.

sections.h2: Which other Nash County Register of Deeds services touch a sale?
sections.html:
Sellers closing an estate or a move often need a few small items from the same counter. The schedule lists them with their prices.

  • Certified birth or death certificate: $10.00 each.
  • Marriage license: $60.00, and a certified marriage copy is $10.00.
  • Notary oath: $10.00, and authentication of a notary: $5.00.
  • Genealogy copy: $1.00 by mail or $0.10 in the office.

Ask the office which of these an estate sale needs, since the right papers depend on how title passed to the seller.

G.S. 47-18 says an unrecorded conveyance, option or longer lease does not bind lien creditors or later buyers who paid value, and priority follows the order in which documents are registered. For a seller, that means an old unrecorded deed or an unfiled loan release can stall a closing.

Cancelling a deed of trust is free to record under the schedule above. If a lender cannot be traced, a North Carolina attorney is the right person to advise on the cleanup.

sections.h2: What does Nash County housing look like in the Census?
sections.html:
Nash County had 99,365 residents in the July 2025 estimate, 4.6% above the 2020 base, living on 540.44 square miles of land. There were 45,068 housing units in 2025, and 63.6% of homes were owner-occupied in 2020 to 2024.

Median value for an owner-occupied unit was $191,000, median monthly rent was $953 and median household income was $62,426. The county issued 483 building permits in 2025, and 21.7% of residents were 65 or older. Veterans numbered 5,784.

faqs.q: What is the phone number for the Nash County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: The county's e-recording page lists (252) 459-9836. Use it to ask about filing, the Memorandum of Understanding or older land records.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a Nash County deed?
faqs.a: The county schedule prints $26.00 for the first 15 pages and $4.00 for each added page. A deed that fails the paper rules adds $25.00.

faqs.q: Does the Nash County Register of Deeds charge to record a loan release?
faqs.a: No. Satisfaction instruments are listed with no fee, so clearing an old deed of trust costs nothing to record.

faqs.q: Which Nash County town offices issue zoning permits before building?
faqs.a: Bailey, Castalia, Dortches, Middlesex, Momeyer, Nashville, Red Oak, Sharpsburg, Spring Hope and Whitakers. The county issues its construction permits only after the town permit.

faqs.q: How are excise stamps charged on a Nash County sale?
faqs.a: The schedule lists $1.00 per $500, and the seller owes the tax before the deed is recorded.
